findings.defect: The proposition asserts "There are one-player stopping SSGs ... whose all-switches runs have length 9 and 12", but nothing beyond a HARMONIC NORMAL FORM is exhibited or verified. The normal-form -> game direction is the paper's (v4), listed UNVERIFIED, and the standing rules say a route needing the dyadic binary-expansion chain of sec:fold "must implement and verify it itself". The root agent's pipeline did build explicit games at m=3 (58 vertices, B1_game.json) and m=4 (AP_m4_*_game.json, N=100); this route did not at m=5,6. findings.defect: PROBABLE UNLABELLED PRIOR ART. The route attributes the DEFINITION of deformed products to Amenta and Ziegler but presents the rigidity lemma as its own. That the fibre of a deformed product over a vertex of the base is normally equivalent to the last factor is, from memory (unchecked against the source), the defining property of the Amenta–Ziegler construction, not a consequence discovered here. Separately, the deformed-CUBE case of the theorem is a three-line observation and should be stated as such: writing the cube as l_i(x_<i) <= x_i <= u_i(x_<i), the fibre in x_d is a segment, genericity forces c_d != 0, so coordinate d is UNIFORM ("combed"), one bottom-antipodal step drives every vertex into the facet it points to, and the facet is again a deformed cube. That combed-and-recursively-combed orientations have BA height <= d is folklore-adjacent in the USO literature. The block generalisation is the only part that needs the normal-fan argument.
findings.evidence: The route's own rem:hcube-notallcubes concedes the mechanism ("for a deformed cube that block is a single uniform coordinate"). I verified the uniform-coordinate consequence directly: t_deform.py's own output line "violations of 'last coordinate uniform + facet is the induced deformed cube': 0".

findings.result_name: rem:hcube-dprod-check (the corroboration of thm:hcube-dprod on random deformed cubes)
findings.defect: THE RANDOM CORROBORATION IS UNINFORMATIVE AND THE REMARK OVERSTATES IT. "no instance ever exceeded the bound d over several thousand random instances in dimensions 2 to 7" is true but vacuous: every random deformed cube sampled has BA height at most 2, so the bound d is never approached, and the one test that tried to push the height produced NO valid instance at all at d >= 6. The instance set does not vary the parameter the theorem turns on; the only instances attaining the bound are the classical ones. (This does not affect the theorem, which is proved; it affects the honesty of the sentence.)
findings.evidence: I re-ran t_deform.py: "d=2..6: 400 nondegenerate samples, max BA height 2"; "d=7: 120 nondegenerate samples, max BA height 2" — 2120 samples, not "several thousand", all of height 2. logs/deform2.log (the stress test t_deform2.py, which asserts h <= d in code): "d=6: best height found -1 ... d=7: -1 ... d=8: -1", i.e. zero instances survived the validity filter at those dimensions.

findings.defect: NEARLY VACUOUS AS A RESULT. The criterion is the definition of LP-realisability written out, and the route concedes that its worked instance settles nothing new ("That this class is LP-realisable follows already from prop:oneplayer-lp"). Its only function is to calibrate a program that then fails on the five open classes. findings.defect: THE GAP IS SOFTER THAN THE TRUTH, AND ITS ADVERTISED PAYOFF IS TOO HIGH. (G1) — h*_HK(m+2) >= 2 h*_HK(m) + 2 — would NOT make "an LP-realisable, and perhaps one-player, exponential all-switches family the next construction to build". Holt–Klee is necessary and not sufficient for LP-realisability (Gärtner–Morris–Rüst, which the route cites itself in rem:hcube-five), so an exponentially tall Holt–Klee family need not be an LP orientation of anything; and even a family of LP orientations says nothing about the SIZE of games realising it, which prop:auso-size and rem:blowup-realise identify as the actual obstacle (the standing brief: "N' <= N^c per level is NOT enough"). The true remaining gap is stated below.

findings.result_name: Circularity, barriers, classes, families — none claimed, and none smuggled in
findings.defect: For the record: the route claims no algorithm, no oracle, no polynomial class and no lower-bound family, so the standard failure modes do not apply. thm:hcube-dprod is a negative result about a class of CONSTRUCTIONS, not a barrier: it covers NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi, and must not be filed among the barriers of sec:gap. Its scope is also narrower than "the classical arsenal": it needs every factor to be combinatorially a cube, so it does not cover Amenta–Ziegler's deformed products of polygons, and it does not cover the USO-based long-path constructions (Morris, Friedmann–Hansen–Zwick) that are not LP orientations of deformed products.
findings.evidence: thm:hcube-dprod's hypotheses; rem:hcube-notallcubes concedes the theorem does not reach X(G) and hence not the pivot.

verdict:
NET POSITIVE BUT SMALL, AND IT MUST BE TRIMMED HARD BEFORE INTEGRATION; ONE MEASURED CLAIM IS FALSE.

WHAT IS NEW AND WORTH INTEGRATING (three items).
(1) lem:hcube-stack + lem:hcube-blowfaces + cor:hcube-parity + cor:hcube-transl. This is the route's real contribution and it is correct — I re-derived all of it independently. It upgrades the paper's isolated observation "B^2 is not Holt-Klee" (rem:blowup-measured) into a theorem: B(s,z) is Holt-Klee only if (P) h mod 2 is unbalanced or parity-separating on every 2-face and (T) no 2-face has F and G both with source adjacent to sink on opposite edges; (P) does not mention z, and no height-maximal seed at m=3 or m=4 satisfies it; and no outer coordinate of a blow-up is ever uniform, so every iterate of B from the second on fails Holt-Klee and, by prop:oneplayer-lp, has no nondegenerate one-player realisation at any level. That is a clean closure of the one-player route to thm:blowup's family, and it explains blowhk.py's failure that the paper currently reports as a bare measurement. Integrate.
(2) thm:hcube-dprod + lem:hcube-rigid + prop:hcube-km + rem:hcube-notallcubes. Correct, and it converts the paper's one-sentence Klee-Minty datum at line 4901 into a proof covering every deformed product with cube factors. Integrate, but (i) state plainly that the deformed-cube case is the three-line "combed" argument, (ii) attribute the rigidity lemma to Amenta-Ziegler as its defining property (from memory, unchecked), (iii) drop the Goldfarb-Sit row as a rescaling of Klee-Minty, (iv) cut the random-sample corroboration or say the samples all have height 2, and (v) file it as a closed construction avenue, NOT as a barrier — it covers none of M1-M6 or def:bsi.
(3) h*_1(5) >= 9 and h*_1(6) >= 12 with the two explicit harmonic normal forms, which I verified exactly. But the proposition must either build the two SSGs or be restated as a statement about harmonic normal forms, since the normal-form-to-game step is the paper's unverified (v4).

WHAT MUST NOT BE INTEGRATED. prop:hcube-hkfive (already the paper's prop:hkfive, same witness); the m<=3 and m=4 clauses of prop:hcube-oneplayer (already cor:hstar-one, and stronger there — ties allowed); prop:hcube-lp4 (a definition unrolled, certifying a class already known realisable); rem:hcube-five (no progress; the five classes are already rem:hk-survey). And prop:hcube-blowbest's twisted-product clause must be DELETED: I refuted it. lem:hstar-super applied with the height-11 witness as the FIRST block and the 1-cube as the second, z=1, gives a Holt-Klee AUSO of the 6-cube of BA height 12, and once more gives one of the 7-cube of height 13 — so the table entries should read h*_HK(6) >= 12 and h*_HK(7) >= 13, both following from prop:hkfive with no game, and the one-player games' contribution at m=6 is to h*_LP and h*_1, not to h*_HK.

THE TRUE REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it. Not "(G1) h*_HK(m+2) >= 2h*_HK(m)+2", which even if true would deliver neither an LP orientation (Holt-Klee is necessary, not sufficient) nor a game of polynomial size. The gap is: whether h*_1(m) — the greatest all-switches run length of a stopping one-player SSG on m Max vertices — grows superpolynomially, AND is attained by games on m^{O(1)} vertices; the route adds the two data points h*_1(5) >= 9, h*_1(6) >= 12 to the paper's exact 1, 2, 4, 6, exhibits no growth mechanism, and its headline theorem provably does not touch the occupancy polytope where the answer lives. The whole table 1, 2, 4, 6, >=9, >=12 remains consistent with h*_1(m) = O(m), which would make the one-player half of the pivot (Howard's rule on two-action MDPs, the Melekopoglou-Condon question) polynomial; nothing in this route moves that either way.

VERIFICATION HONESTY: good, with two exceptions. The route correctly labels its lower bounds as lower bounds, correctly declares the LP search on the five classes non-discriminating (1 of 10 controls closed), correctly flags Goldfarb-Sit as reconstructed from memory, and correctly states (P),(T) as necessary only. The exceptions are the false twisted-product measurement (one order of an asymmetric construction tested) and the empty random-sample corroboration of thm:hcube-dprod.
